conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand a bit about your child (or children). 

**First, could you tell me:**
1. Do you have a child or children you're claiming for?
2. What is your child's age (or their ages if you have multiple children)?

This is important because eligibility depends on whether the child is:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old (where education/training matters)
- 20 or over (which would make them ineligible)

Please share your child's name(s) and age(s) so I can guide you through the right path.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me help you with Alex's eligibility.

Since Alex is 15 years old (under 16), he falls into the automatic qualification age category. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news so far! Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is a standard requirement - children in full-time work (24+ hours per week) who aren't in approved education or training aren't eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all. He's still in school full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in school and not working, so that's fine. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

In other words, does Alex claim any benefits personally? (This would be unusual for a 15-year-old, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular school student.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship program?**

Different rules apply depending on the location and type:
- English apprenticeships (all types) would disqualify him
- Scottish Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify him
- Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (but other Welsh apprenticeships would disqualify)

Since you mentioned he's in regular school, I'm assuming he's not in an apprenticeship - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct, he's not in any apprenticeship. He's just doing his regular GCSEs at school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular school doing his GCSEs, so no apprenticeship concerns. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check your residency status. 

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You'll qualify if **ANY** of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the most common situation
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources (and not claiming certain benefits)
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do you normally live in the UK, or does any other situation above apply to you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. I do have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly fine! You meet the residency requirement in **multiple ways** actually:

1. You normally live in the UK (in Manchester) - which satisfies the main path
2. You also have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme - which can provide additional qualifying routes

Since you meet the residency requirements, let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You'll qualify if **ANY** of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you mentioned earlier that he lives with you at home)
2. You contribute to his upkeep by paying at least as much as Child Benefit towards his care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance for him under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home, I believe you meet the first path. Can you confirm that Alex lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you're responsible for him. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else who might have made a claim

Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at a time. If someone else is claiming but you both agree that you should claim instead, that can be arranged. If there's a dispute, HMRC would need to decide.

So, is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! No one else is claiming for Alex, so that's clear. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You mentioned he lives at home with you, but I need to confirm there are no special circumstances.

**Which of these situations applies to Alex?**

1. **Living normally at home with you** (this seems to be your situation)
2. Currently in hospital
3. In local authority care
4. Being fostered

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you. Is that correct, or is there any special living arrangement I should know about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is living normally at home with me. There's no special arrangement or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just one final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing any financial support specifically for Alex's housing or upkeep? (This would be unusual since he lives with you at home, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. He just lives with me and I support him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me proceed to the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
# 🎉 **Great News - You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

Based on all the information you've provided, **you meet all the criteria for Child Benefit for Alex**.

## Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - He's 15 years old (under 16)  
✅ **Employment status** - Alex isn't working (he's in full-time school)  
✅ **No benefits in own right** - Alex doesn't receive ESA or Universal Credit  
✅ **Not in apprenticeship** - He's doing regular GCSEs at school  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives with you at home  
✅ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming for Alex  
✅ **Normal living arrangements** - Alex lives at home with you  
✅ **No council support** - The council isn't paying for Alex's care  

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earn over £60,000, you may need to pay some or all of it back through tax
5. **Payments** - Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

📋 **More information and to apply:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?

(4) Apprenticeship: Alex is not in any apprenticeship program - he is doing his regular GCSEs at school. (5) Claimant residency: The claimant normally lives in the UK (Manchester) and meets residency requirements. (6) Responsibility: The claimant lives with Alex and is responsible for him. (7) No competing claim: No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. (8) Living situation: Alex lives normally at home with the claimant with no special arrangements. (9) Council support: The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All criteria are satisfied.
